title: LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's recommended workspace_id derivation ($env:COMPUTERNAME + "-loop") collides across parallel workspaces on the same host, defeating the GH-issue lock
discovered_in: WF03-GH542-20260807 (incidental finding, surfaced by the user during post-incident review of the GH-542 collision fix)
symptom: Both this workspace and a sibling parallel checkout of the same repo on the same machine derived the identical workspace_id 'TVOLODI-loop' when following LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's own documented example ($env:COMPUTERNAME + "-loop"). This is a distinct defect from the missing-immediate-push race (ISS/PR #543): even with the claim pushed to main immediately, two workspaces claiming under the SAME workspace_id key makes the lock's audit trail unable to distinguish which physical checkout is doing the work, and (more importantly) a workspace_id collision means log lines and any future collision-detection logic that keys off workspace_id cannot tell the two apart.
root_cause: $env:COMPUTERNAME (Windows machine name) is identical for every checkout on one physical host. This repo has a standing, documented parallel-workspace pattern (see .env's own header: 'SECOND parallel workspace', COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=r-co-2, +10 port band) specifically because multiple checkouts on one machine is a normal, expected setup here -- but LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's workspace_id guidance was written as if one host runs one workspace, and was never updated when the two-workspace-per-host pattern became standard practice.
impact: Any two parallel workspaces on this host that both enter loop mode produce colliding lock-owner identities. Combined with ISS-0543 (the missing-immediate-push race), this was part of why GH-542 was claimed by two workspaces simultaneously -- though it is a separate, independently-triggerable defect: even a correctly-immediate push does not prevent the collision, it only changes which workspace's identical-looking claim wins the race.
evidence: docs/agents/protocols/LOOP_PROTOCOL.md line 172 (pre-fix): '$workspace_id = $env:COMPUTERNAME + "-loop"   # e.g. "TVOLODI-loop"'. tools/gh_claim.py line 21 (pre-fix): 'Use a stable value (e.g. machine name)'. Both this workspace (c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\2\R-Co) and the sibling (c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co) run on host TVOLODI and would derive 'TVOLODI-loop' identically from either recipe.
fix_target: Introduce BPM_WORKSPACE_ID as a per-checkout .env variable (set by hand, following the existing COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME convention for parallel-workspace isolation), document it in .env.example, and update LOOP_PROTOCOL.md + gh_claim.py's docstring to read it instead of deriving from $env:COMPUTERNAME.
related_issues: GH-542 / ISS-0607 -- the incident this was discovered while reviewing
The missing-immediate-push race fixed in PR #543 -- a separate, compounding defect in the same loop-mode locking flow
resolution: Added BPM_WORKSPACE_ID as a documented .env.example variable, set by hand per checkout (this workspace's own .env now sets BPM_WORKSPACE_ID=r-co-2-loop, reusing the existing COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME value). LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's 'ORCH loop mode' section now reads BPM_WORKSPACE_ID from .env with an explicit failure if unset, instead of deriving from $env:COMPUTERNAME. Both LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's tools-reference section and gh_claim.py's own docstring now warn against machine-name-derived workspace_id values and point at BPM_WORKSPACE_ID instead.
